summary: Lake Superior light off Rossport, Ontario, lit 1877 under keeper Charles McKay; boat access only, and visits suspended since July 2025.

staffing.note: Last keeper, Bert Saasto, retired November 1991 (LighthouseFriends).

access.note: Reached only by boat. DFO suspended the Friends' agreement in July 2025 for a review; the island is closed to visitors (Lighthouse Directory).

events.note: Department of Marine contracts Joseph White for the Battle Island and Lamb Island lights.
Lit 27 August 1877 under keeper Charles McKay.
Steamer Ontario aground in dense fog on the island; total wreck; crew rescued.
Hand fog horn supplied to the station.
Position of the lighthouse corrected on the charts.
Edward McKay succeeds his father, Charles McKay.
Octagonal tower replaces the first wooden tower; lit 12 May 1915.
Diaphone fog alarm building; standard fog alarm listed in the 1914-15 report.
Three flashes in a 24-second cycle, petroleum vapour burner under a mantle.
Keeper Malcolm Sutherland drowns in August; LighthouseFriends records the only fatality on the island.
November gale, as recalled by keeper Bert Saasto; waves reached the lantern.
Last keeper Bert Saasto retires; no keeper on duty afterwards.
DFO suspends the Friends' agreement at the end of July for a review; island closed to visitors.

keepers.name: Charles Stephen McKay
keepers.note: Appointed by Order in Council in September 1876 at $500 a year; first lit the light 27 August 1877. LighthouseFriends counts 36 seasons. The 1906 statement (scan 174, printed p. 165) lists 'McKay, Chas. S' at Battle Island, appointed Aug. 27, 1877, 500 00: checked on the page image.

keepers.name: Andrew Dick
keepers.note: Kept the light from 2 to 27 August 1877 until McKay arrived. Later served at Porphyry Point.

keepers.name: Edward McKay
keepers.note: Son of Charles McKay; replaced his father. The 1913-14 statement (scan 74, printed p. 67) lists 'E. McKay' at Battle island, appointed April 4, 1913: checked on the page image.

keepers.name: Mrs. Malcolm Sutherland
keepers.note: Widow who served out the rest of the 1932 season. LighthouseFriends roster gives 1932-1933.

keepers.name: George Brady
keepers.note: Keeper during the 1953-54 moose episode, as LighthouseFriends reports.

keepers.name: Bert Saasto
keepers.note: Last keeper; retired November 1991. LighthouseFriends roster gives 1991 only, so the start of his service is not known. Later volunteer caretaker and interpreter.

wrecks.outcome: Ran aground in dense fog on the island; total wreck; crew rescued.

corrections.field: events: built 1911 (Lighthouse Directory year of tower)
corrections.why: The octagonal tower that replaced the first wooden one was placed in operation on 12 May 1915 (LighthouseFriends); the 1914-15 Department report lists a fog alarm at the station. No source we read supports 1911.
The first light was shown 27 August 1877 (LighthouseFriends, quoting the 1877 report). The 1911 date matches the later tower, not a first light.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: Three sources give different characteristics because the light changed. The 1915 light showed three flashes in a 24-second cycle (Fl(3) W 24s in Wikidata, LighthouseFriends); the current Coast Guard list gives Fl W 10s. The date of the change is not in any source we read.

The 1877 light was seen 18 miles and elevated 105 feet; the current Coast Guard figures are a 10 nautical mile range and a 36.0 m focal height. These describe different lights, one of them the later structure.

notes_for_editor:
Sources. The pre-1900 Canadian record is not in the local corpus (marine_ca covers fiscal 1900 to 1924 only). The 1877 and 1885 Department descriptions, the contract and the keeper roster from 1877 to 1911 come from LighthouseFriends, which quotes the Department's reports; they are cited as second-hand and should be checked against the originals if they become available. Keeper roster lines from 1922 to 1991 rest on LighthouseFriends alone. The 1899 wreck, the 1932 drowning and the moose episode are also LighthouseFriends only; Chronicling America searches for Battle Island found no hits.

OCR table rows, checked on the scan images on 2026-10-28 (not only the OCR): (a) 1913-14 statement, scan 74 (printed p. 67): '*Battle island | E. McKay | April 4, 1913 | 600 00': confirmed, and the story now gives the full date. (b) 1906 statement, scan 174 (printed p. 165): 'McKay, Chas. S | Battle Island | Aug. 27, 1877 | 500 00': confirmed, and the story now gives the full date. (c) 1914-15 'Changes and Improvements in Existing Aids', scan 58 (printed p. 51): the Battle island row reads 'Erection of standard fog alarm building, double dwelling, 30 ft. reinforced concrete tower, 8 ft. cast iron lantern, triple flash long focus reflector and 35 mm. burner. (Work will be completed next year.)', day labour, foreman M. J. Egan and J. Montgomery, $12,173.54. The story quotes the work list only, not the foreman or cost columns.

Disagreements the sources do not settle. Tower material: the 1914-15 table says reinforced concrete; LighthouseFriends gives an octagonal tower and no material; the Lighthouse Directory says 13 m 'concrete' (not re-read on this check). Tower height: the record has 13.0 m (OSM), Coast Guard 13.1 m, the 1877 tower 30 feet, the 1914 plan 'thirty-foot' (LighthouseFriends), and the 1914-15 table 30 ft. Fog signal: the 1914-15 table says a standard fog alarm building; LighthouseFriends says a diaphone. First year: 1877 (LighthouseFriends, Directory 'station established 1877') against 1911 (Wikidata, the Directory's tower year). Characteristic: current Fl W 10s; the change from the 1915 three-flash pattern is undated. Access: the record says 'unknown'; the Directory says 'closed to visitors' in its text and keeps 'Site open, tower closed' in its standard line. The 2025 suspension in SNNewsWatch (22 December 2025) is the most recent source; the editor should confirm the current position with DFO before the Today section goes live.

Units. Canadian figures are metres first in the story, with the source's feet or miles in brackets.

People. Keepers after about 1960 (Brady, Hubelit, Joiner, Saasto) are named only as LighthouseFriends names them, in their public role; the health detail LighthouseFriends gives for Saasto is left out. The widow's family is not named beyond her husband's name.

Not done: the Friends of Battle Island Lighthouse site (battleisland.ca) was not read; no photos were added.
